title: Position-dependent tight-binding model for Li impurities in monolayer and bilayer graphene
authors: Hernan Aguirre, Hernan L. Calvo, Eduardo M. Perassi
abstract: Lithium adsorption and intercalation can significantly modify the low-energy electronic properties of graphene-based materials, making their characterization relevant for understanding Li-ion transport and storage in graphitic electrodes. In this work, we investigate the electronic structure of a Li ion adsorbed on monolayer graphene (MLG) and intercalated within AB-stacked bilayer graphene (BLG). To this end, we develop a semi-empirical tight-binding model that incorporates Li-position dependence. Its parameters are determined by fitting to density-functional-theory calculations for different configurations, heights, and supercell sizes. The obtained model accurately reproduces the electronic bands near the Fermi level for both MLG and BLG and provides a transparent interpretation of the impurity-induced modifications in terms of symmetry breakings, intervalley mixing, and band-gap openings. We find that the perturbation introduced by the Li ion is strongly localized and that its effect decreases with increasing supercell size. The fitted parameters further reveal systematic differences between MLG and BLG in the spatial profile of the impurity potential. The obtained results provide an efficient framework for studying dilute Li impurities and constitute a useful starting point for future investigations of Li diffusion and impurity-induced transport phenomena in graphene-based materials.
summary: This work develops and validates a position-dependent tight-binding model to study how adsorbed or intercalated Lithium ions alter the electronic structure of graphene (MLG and BLG). By fitting parameters to DFT results, the authors accurately predict band modifications, revealing that Li introduces localized perturbations whose effects diminish as the supercell size increases. This provides an efficient framework for modeling ion transport in graphitic electrodes.
main_problem: The study investigates how Li adsorption on monolayer graphene (MLG) and intercalation within bilayer graphene (BLG) modifies their low-energy electronic properties.
main_result: The developed position-dependent tight-binding model accurately reproduces the band structure, showing that the impurity perturbation is strongly localized and decreases with supercell size.
method: A semi-empirical, position-dependent tight-binding (TB) model is constructed and parameterized by fitting its eigenvalues to results obtained from Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations.
model_or_system: The system involves MLG and AB-stacked BLG substrates doped with Li impurities. The Hamiltonian incorporates site-specific couplings derived from DFT fittings, allowing for the study of impurity effects on electronic bands near the Fermi level.
key_observables: Electronic band structure near the Fermi level, symmetry breakings, intervalley mixing, and band-gap openings.
important_parameters: Supercell size ($n$), Li onsite energy ($\epsilon_{	ext{Li}}$), and various hopping parameters derived from DFT fitting.
main_assumptions: The TB model assumes parameter efficiency by keeping the number of fitting variables constant regardless of impurity position or supercell size.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate supercells for Li adsorption/intercalation on MLG and BLG, high-symmetry k-paths in the Brillouin zone, and schematics detailing the electronic structure analysis.
paper_structure: The paper develops a general TB framework, parameterizes it using DFT calculations across varying supercell sizes, analyzes the resulting band structures for both MLG and BLG, and discusses the physical implications of the localized impurity potential.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter electronics, the development of an accurate, transferable tight-binding model parameterized by first principles methods is a powerful tool for simulating open quantum systems where local perturbations (like impurities) drive transport phenomena.
